I have been farming this land in Quzhou County for 45 years, and at 60 years old I know what works here on the North China Plain. My household has seven people, and with some of the younger ones working off-farm, I cannot manage too much labor-intensive cotton by myself. So this year I will put about 8 mu into the wheat-maize double crop that feeds the family and brings steady income, and keep roughly 2.9 mu for cotton to earn cash. I have a well for irrigation, which means I can water when the crops need it most, but pumping costs money so I will not waste water.

For the winter wheat, I will use an improved variety and rotary tillage before sowing in October. I will apply base fertilizer and then topdress with urea at green-up and jointing, giving about 16 kg of nitrogen per mu in total, plus phosphorus and potassium. I will irrigate three times: once for overwintering, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. I expect around 580 kg per mu if the weather cooperates.

For the summer maize, I will sow a hybrid variety immediately after the wheat harvest in early June. Because the window is tight and labor is short, I will use no-tillage seeding to save time and fuel. I will apply compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress nitrogen at the big trumpet stage, totaling about 16 kg nitrogen per mu. I will irrigate twice—once around tasseling and once at grain filling—and spray pesticides twice if pests show up. I expect about 620 kg per mu.

For the cotton, I will plant a hybrid Bt cotton variety in April. Cotton roots need to go deep, so I will plough the field first. It needs more care than grain, so I will apply about 18 kg nitrogen per mu plus phosphorus and potassium, irrigate three times during flowering and boll development, and spray pesticides five times to control bollworm and aphids. I aim for about 280 kg of seed cotton per mu.
